title.narrative: Support to community-led emergency humanitarian responses in Khartoum, Al Jazeera, North Kordofan, South Kordofan and North Darfur states, Sudan.

description.narrative: ltpgtActed proposes a 12-month project to support Mutual Aid Groups (MAGs) in conflict-affected and hard-to-reach areas of Khartoum, Al Jazeera, North Kordofan, South Kordofan and North Darfur states, Sudan, expecting to reach a total of 35,680 individuals with emergency food and protection assistance. Acted will ensure support for critical food assistance interventions by providing Group Cash Transfers (GCTs) to volunteer-run food assistance initiatives, including Humanitarian Aid Commission (HAC)-registered Takeya in Khartoum and Emergency Response Rooms (ERRs) in Khartoum, North Kordofan, Al Jazeera and North Darfur to enable the provision of essential food items, addressing acute food insecurity for vulnerable populations in frontline and hard-to-reach areas. Acted will support 43 MAGs with a total of 645,000.00 USD, transferring approximately 5,000 USD per round per group based on needs and capacities. Acted estimates reaching 800 individuals per MAG per transfer, contributing to a total of 34,400 beneficiaries under this activity. Acted will also address acute protection risks and needs and strengthen community-led protection initiatives through direct support to the ERRs’ protection interventions in frontline and hard-to-reach areas of Khartoum, Al Jazeera, North Kordofan and North Darfur states. Acted will provide funding in tranches up to 20,000 USD through ERR-led mechanisms to support 1,280 vulnerable individuals, including women, children, and Persons with Specific Needs (PSNs) with Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), either directly in cash or in-kind, at an average of 160 USD per individual. Finally, Acted will strengthen the ERRs’ operational and technical capacity through financial support to cover operational costs needed to provide timely and effective humanitarian response and ad-hoc training to ERR volunteers to address gaps identified during implementation. Acted will provide direct financial support in tranches up to 20,000 USD to state-level ERR Committees in Khartoum, Al Jazeera, North Kordofan, South Kordofan and North Darfur states to facilitate the coordination and implementation of ERR-led assistance activities. Acted works closely with MAGs in frontline areas to ensure that safety and security are considered in the selection of sites. A key component of mitigating the risks that these groups face in hot zone areas, like Al Jazeera state, is the provision of operations costs to support groups in procuring goods and services that allow them to operate safely, including communications devices, transportation costs, and other forms of day-to-day support that prevent volunteers from assuming unnecessary risks. In addition, Acted works closely with the state-level protection offices of MAGs working in frontline areas to identify risks and ensure funding and plans are in place to evacuate volunteers when needed or provide them with funding to access care needed to mitigate potential risks. Given the lack of access that formal organizations have in places like Al Jazeera state, cash programming – specifically GCTs to MAGs – is the most effective way of reaching vulnerable communities.ltbrgtActed works with the Localization Coordination Council (LCC) to select MAGs based on the coverage provided by other actors, the needs on the ground and their capacity to deliver. Acted then assesses the performance of MAGs through the F-system reports to determine if further funding can be allocated and works with locality and state-level LCC representatives to identify groups most in need of support, adapting its implementation according to these priorities. For HAC-registered MAGs, Acted works with HAC to identify existing groups and verify their capacity and functionality, selecting those with a proven track record of delivery and accepted by the community. Under this project, Acted will work with MAGs with whom Acted has a previous relationship, as well as new MAGs identified through LCC engagement.ltbrgtlt/pgt
